title: Foot-patting and keeping time
summary: Hall rarely pats his foot with a good rhythm section; the interviewer notes drummers like Baby Dodds argued against it.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Yeah, sure. One other question. I may have some pretty silly sounding questions to you. There's a few things that some people know that, for instance, like in patting your foot in a band, some people will say it's good to do that. And of course, in their classical symphony, they don't allow people to be a hundred of them patting their foot. You wouldn't hear the music. But in a jazz band, do you, for instance, do you still pat your foot or anything at the same time when you play?

No, no, no, usually I don't pat my foot, not especially if I got a good rhythm section. If I got a good rhythm section. But if I got a bad rhythm section, usually I do. But a lot of times if you're reading music too, you got to count too, you know, you got to pat your foot. Some guys pat four to a bar, some pat two, some pat one. You think it's a good idea for young players or students you might say? Yeah, well then I won't tell you. You get used to it, then you don't have to count. But usually you always, you're following the bar. A lot of times you got a lot of tunes that you play and you got a lot of layout. You got to count those bars out. Sure.

For instance, Shelley won't use to pat his foot a lot. People like Bump did, I know. And other people like Baby Dodge. For person on a drummer he doesn't have to work. He's got that foot going. He's going all the time. Baby's argued with me that Baby Dodge said you shouldn't pat your foot. You shouldn't have to do that.

No you shouldn't. Not if you got a good rhythm. That's right. You shouldn't have to. You can feel it. If you got a good rhythm section, you don't have to worry about the rhythm behind you. behind you. Usually when those guys are not hitting back there together, you can feel it. Then you got to keep your own tempo.
